Many Favor Randolph Plan
By JAMES E. DAVIS
More than 30 persons attended a public hearing on the proposed master plan for the Randolph area of the West End last night at Amelia School, and many indicated favor of the plan.
Spokesmen for The Richmond Redevelopment and Housing Authority said that 1.185 of the 2,2m structures in the area would be scheduled for demolition.
Most of the questions asked by residents of the area concerned relocation payments
and other financial aid they may receive when displaced over the six to eight year life of the project.
Dr. Allix B. James, chairman of the city planning commission, referred residents of the area to an office operated by the housing authority at 1610 Winder St. for more specific information.
The planning commission is scheduled to take action on the master plan Dec. 4, and City Council may hold a public hearing and act early in January
Alan Siff, a consultant for theal housing authority, s that the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) may approve the redevelopment plan in the spring.
"Will people have to move?" several speakers asked.
"There would be some relocation, yes," said Planning Director A. Howe Todd. Blighted areas are to be cleared, streets are to be created by linking Colorado Avenue with Harrison Street
(and the right of way for the Downtown Expressway that has been cleared), west of Riverview Cemetery and north of Colorado Avenue.
Most of the demolition would occur in the northeast quadrant, an area east of Meadow Street, north of Lakeview Avenue, east of and including Harrison Street, and south of the expressway right of way.

Randolph Plan
Richmond Times-Dispatch, Tues., Dec. 5, 1972
Approval Urged
By JAMES E. DAVIS
The City yesterday approval of Planning Commission recommended a new master plan for the Randolph area of the West End.
In preparation for more than three years by city officials and residents of the area, the plan now goes to City Council for possible approval.
'It calls for the demolition of 1,185 of the area's 2,290 structures. More than 300 persons attended a recent public hearing held at Amelia School by the City Planning Commission and most of them indicated that the general redevelopment plan should be approved. It would bring new housing, a better traffic pattern and designated snopping areas.
Possible Impact
Mrs. Douglas C. Burke, a commission member, abstained in the voting yesterday, saying that she is concerned over the possible impact on the area of the proposed Downtown Expressway. The Randolph area is generally east of Byrd Park, south of Cary Street, north of Colorado Avenue and west of Riveryew Cemetery.
An unused portion of the cemetery would be needed for a new link between Colorado Avenue and Harrison Street,
the planners said. Harrison Street would be widened and improved, as would Meadow Street, to serve as one of the major tratfic arteries for the Randolph area.
